exceptions.reason: Screen-reader-only text (table captions, severity and unread labels) is clipped to 1px on purpose. Its size is never seen, so the type scale does not apply (the Counter keeps its h1 for screen readers only).
Stacked phone tables keep their header row for screen readers only; each cell shows its own label.
Segments share one inset track (DESIGN.md segmented control); the 2px seam is the design, and each segment meets the size rules.

The chosen segment's paper is one sliding highlight drawn behind the options (motion.css, selectionPills.ts), so the tool cannot read a background. The colours are unchanged: --ink on --surface for the chosen one, --ink-muted on --fill for the rest, which src/theme/contrast.test.ts checks pass 4.5:1.

The sign-in notes float over the sunrise drawing, so the tool cannot read a background behind them. They sit on 85% paper with --ink and --ink-muted text, which src/theme/contrast.test.ts checks pass 4.5:1 on --surface.
The clay key is lit by a soft light gradient (DESIGN.md 8, Light), so the tool cannot measure it. Its text is --cta-ink on --cta, which src/theme/contrast.test.ts checks passes 4.5:1.

The two product cards on Possible duplicates are raised panels lit by the sheen and light gradients (DESIGN.md 8, Light), so the tool cannot read their background. Measured on the flat fill: muted text 4.76:1 light, 6.14:1 dark; ink 13.3:1 and 12.2:1.
The accounts an entry touches, as account numbers (codes like 1110, 4000), not amounts; they read left to right like a list.
The previous/next arrows beside a month or year menu: the arrow beside the month name says what it does, and each has an aria-label and a title for mouse users.

The Counter bar, till tape and keys are raised paper lit from above by --light-raise (DESIGN.md 8, Light), a white wash that only lightens the paper, so the tool cannot read a background. The text is --ink and --ink-muted on --surface or --fill, which src/theme/contrast.test.ts checks pass 4.5:1.

The sheet panel is lit by the same light gradient, and the centred question rises in over the page, so the tool cannot read its background. The text is --ink and --ink-muted on --surface, which src/theme/contrast.test.ts checks pass 4.5:1.

A field's hint or a short note inside a sheet (the Counter's opening cash, drawer count and PIN sheets) sits on the same gradient-lit sheet panel, so the tool cannot read it. The text is --ink-muted on --surface, which src/theme/contrast.test.ts checks passes 4.5:1.
The X in every sheet corner: a universal close mark with an aria-label, and Esc does the same.

The download page cards, the printer check and the welcome choice cards are raised panels lit by --light-raise (DESIGN.md 8, Light), so the tool cannot read their background. Their text is --ink and --ink-muted on --surface (or --tint), which src/theme/contrast.test.ts checks pass 4.5:1.
The Counter's Pay key shows the amount to pay at the figure size (28px, on the type scale), so the person at the till reads it from a step away. The key's label stays at 15px.
The arrow and plus/minus keys in the Counter's shortcut legend are symbols, so contrast can't be measured; they use the same ink on paper as the lettered keys beside them, which pass.

On a phone the Counter bar keys (Switch person, Home, Log out) shrink to their icons: the label is hidden on purpose the visually-hidden way (1px, clip-path), and each button keeps its aria-label and title.
The Counter basket's Code column holds barcodes and SKUs (LGT-LAMP-BRS, 3830009876543): identifiers read left to right, not amounts to compare.
On phones the closed menu drawer waits off-screen to the left and slides in when opened; it is hidden from view, not cut off.
Words inside a visually-hidden block (a chart's figures as a list for screen readers) are hidden on purpose, like the block itself.

On a phone the Steps bar shows only the current step's name; the others are hidden the visually-hidden way (1px, clip-path) and stay readable to screen readers. Steps you can go back to show their name in a tooltip.
Calendar days are dates laid out in a month grid, read across the week; they are not amounts in a column to compare.
On a phone each planned thing in a calendar day is drawn as a 6px dot and its words are pushed out of sight on purpose; the day key still reads them out.
